definitions.explanation: Reading quickly by letting the eyes flow over the text without carefully reading every word, picking up the general meaning or key points.

examples.japanese: {記事|きじ}を{流|なが}し{読|よ}みする。
{時間|じかん}がなかったので、{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{流|なが}し{読|よ}みした。
examples.english: I didn't have time, so I skimmed the report.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}し{読|よ}みでは{大事|だいじ}なポイントを{見落|みお}とすことがあるので、{契約書|けいやくしょ}はしっかり{読|よ}むべきだ。
examples.english: Skimming can cause you to miss important points, so you should read contracts carefully.

notes:
A compound of {流|なが}す (to let flow) and {読|よ}み (reading). The image is of letting your eyes "flow" over the text rather than stopping to absorb each word. The verb form is {流|なが}し{読|よ}みする.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {流|なが}し{読|よ}みする: to skim-read
- {流|なが}し{読|よ}みで{済|す}ませる: to get by with just skimming
- ざっと{流|なが}し{読|よ}みする: to quickly skim through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming, reading diagonally — similar meaning, another common word for reading quickly
- {速読|そくどく}: speed reading — implies a trained technique for reading quickly while retaining comprehension
- {精読|せいどく}: close reading — the opposite: reading carefully and thoroughly
